legal.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
legal.privacy.summary: What Mahaam collects across the web, mobile, desktop and browser apps, why, who else handles it, and how to delete it.
legal.terms.title: Terms of Service
legal.terms.summary: The agreement for using Mahaam on the web, on your phone, on your desktop and in your browser.
legal.terms.agreement.heading: Agreement
legal.terms.agreement.body:
These terms are an agreement between you and Mahaam for your use of Mahaam: the web app, the **Mahaam** mobile app for iOS and Android, the desktop tray app, the browser extension, the API and the MCP server (together, "the service"). By creating an account or using the service you accept these terms and our Privacy Policy.

If you use Mahaam for a company or another organisation, you accept these terms on its behalf and confirm that you're allowed to. If you download the mobile app from the App Store or Google Play, the store's own terms also apply to the download, but this agreement is between you and Mahaam, not Apple or Google.
legal.terms.accounts.heading: Your account
legal.terms.accounts.body:
You must be at least 16 to create an account. Give accurate information and keep your email address current, because that's where we send security messages.

Keep your password, recovery codes and access tokens safe; we recommend turning on two-factor authentication. You're responsible for what's done with your account and your tokens, including by AI agents and apps you connect. An account is for one person, so don't share your sign-in. Tell us at once at [info@3x1.io](mailto:info@3x1.io) if you think someone else has access.
legal.terms.workspaces.heading: Workspaces and roles
legal.terms.workspaces.body:
Work in Mahaam happens in workspaces. A workspace belongs to its owners, who decide who joins it and with which role:

- **Owner**: full control of the workspace, including its plan and billing, its members and roles, and deleting it.
- **Admin**: manages members, settings and every project.
- **Project manager**: runs the projects they manage, including tasks, time, budgets and reports.
- **Employee**: works on the projects they're part of and tracks their own time.
- **Customer**: someone outside the team, such as a client, who sees only the workspace's customer portal and what the workspace shares there.

The exact permissions of each role are shown in the app and may change as Mahaam develops. Owners are responsible for whom they invite and which role they give. If you join a workspace, the work you do there belongs to the workspace, and it stays with the workspace if you leave.
legal.terms.content.heading: Your content
legal.terms.content.body:
You and your workspace keep all rights to the content you put into Mahaam: projects, tasks, issues, comments, files, time entries, invoices and everything else. We don't claim ownership of it.

You give us permission to host, copy, process, transmit and display that content only as needed to provide, secure and support the service for you and your workspace. We don't sell it, and we don't use it to train AI models. Content that a customer submits through a workspace's portal or feedback widget belongs to that workspace, subject to any agreement between them.

You're responsible for having the right to upload what you upload, and for the personal data about other people that your workspace stores, such as your clients' contact details. If you send us feedback or suggestions, we may use them without any obligation to you.
legal.terms.use.heading: Acceptable use
legal.terms.plans.heading: Paid plans and payment
legal.terms.plans.body:
Some features and quotas depend on the workspace's plan. Paid plans are sold through **Polar**, which acts as our **merchant of record**: Polar is the seller on your receipt, processes the payment, and handles sales tax or VAT, invoices and refunds under its own terms. If a workspace subscribes through GitHub Marketplace, GitHub bills it instead.

Subscriptions renew automatically at the end of each billing period until they're cancelled. An owner can cancel at any time, and the plan stays active until the end of the period already paid for. Prices are shown before you pay, and we'll tell owners before a price change applies to them. Usage beyond a plan's quota is billed or limited as shown on the plan page. Except where the law or Polar's refund policy says otherwise, fees already paid aren't refunded. If a payment fails, we may limit the workspace after telling its owners.
legal.terms.availability.heading: Availability and changes
legal.terms.availability.body: We work to keep Mahaam available and your data safe, but we can't promise that the service will never be interrupted. We may change, add or remove features. If a change takes away something you rely on, we'll tell you in advance where we can.
legal.terms.thirdparty.heading: Other services
legal.terms.thirdparty.body: Mahaam can connect to services such as GitHub, Jira, Linear and Google, and the mobile app is distributed through Apple's and Google's app stores. Those services have their own terms, and we aren't responsible for them. Connecting one lets Mahaam use the access you grant, only to provide the feature you turned on.
legal.terms.termination.heading: Ending
legal.terms.termination.body:
You can stop using Mahaam and delete your account at any time, as the Privacy Policy describes. If you're the only owner of a workspace, you'll need to hand it over or delete it first. Deleting a workspace deletes its content.

We may suspend or close an account or a workspace that breaks these terms, that puts the service or other people at risk, or where the law requires it. We'll tell you why unless the law or safety prevents it, and where we reasonably can, we'll give you a chance to fix the problem or export your content first.

The parts of these terms that by their nature should last, such as those on content, disclaimers and liability, continue after your account ends.
legal.terms.disclaimers.heading: Disclaimers
legal.terms.disclaimers.body:
The service is provided "as is" and "as available". To the extent the law allows, we make no warranties of any kind, express or implied, including warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement.

We don't promise that the service will be error-free or uninterrupted, or that the totals, reports and invoices it calculates are free of mistakes. Check them before you rely on them, for example before you send an invoice to a client. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under consumer law that can't be excluded.
legal.terms.liability.heading: Limitation of liability
legal.terms.liability.body:
To the extent the law allows, Mahaam isn't liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for any loss of profits, revenue, data or goodwill, arising from your use of the service.

Our total liability for all claims relating to the service is limited to the amount paid for the service in the 12 months before the event that gave rise to the claim. These limits don't apply where the law doesn't allow them to.
legal.terms.changes.heading: Changes to these terms
legal.terms.changes.body: When we change these terms we update the date at the top of this page. If a change matters, we'll tell you in the app or by email before it takes effect. If you keep using Mahaam after that, you accept the new terms; if you don't agree, you can stop using the service and delete your account.
legal.terms.contact.heading: Contact and notices
legal.terms.contact.body: Questions about these terms, and legal notices to us, go to [info@3x1.io](mailto:info@3x1.io). Notices we send you go to the email address on your account, or appear in the app.
legal.privacy.short.heading: The short version
legal.privacy.short.body:
Mahaam keeps your team's projects, tasks, issues and time so that your team can use them. We don't sell your data and we don't show you ads.

This policy covers every way you use Mahaam: the web app, the **Mahaam** mobile app for iOS and Android, the desktop tray app, the browser extension, the API and the MCP server. You can delete your account from inside the app, and you can reach us at [info@3x1.io](mailto:info@3x1.io).
legal.privacy.who.heading: Who is responsible
legal.privacy.who.body:
In this policy "Mahaam", "we" and "us" mean the operator of the Mahaam service. We decide how your **account data** is used.

The work stored in a **workspace** (the company or team that uses Mahaam) is controlled by that workspace: its owners decide who can see it, and we process it on their behalf. If you have a question about work stored in someone else's workspace, ask its owners first.
legal.privacy.account.heading: Your account
legal.privacy.account.body:
**What we keep.** Your name and email address, and your password, stored only as a salted one-way hash (bcrypt), never in plain text. Optionally a profile picture, your language and your timezone.

**Two-factor authentication (optional).** If you turn it on, we store your authenticator secret encrypted, your one-time recovery codes only as hashes that we can't read back, and a count of recent wrong codes so that guessing is limited.

**Why.** To sign you in and keep your account secure, to email you what you asked for (a sign-up confirmation, a password reset code, invitations and the notifications you chose), and to show you to your teammates.
legal.privacy.work.heading: Your workspace content
legal.privacy.work.body:
What you and your team put into a workspace: projects, issues, tasks, comments, attachments and screenshots, clients, requests, invoices and reports.

It's stored so the workspace can use it, and it's visible only to the people the workspace's owners allow, according to their role. We don't look at it except to keep the service running, to fix a problem you've asked us to look at, or when the law requires it.
legal.privacy.time.heading: Time tracking
legal.privacy.time.body:
Timers you start and stop and time you log by hand, with the project, task and description you chose, the start and end times, and the rate that applied when the entry was created (so an invoice doesn't change later).

The desktop tray app notices when your computer has been idle so it can ask whether to keep that time. It reads only **how long** the system has been idle. It never records which apps, windows or websites you use, and it never takes screenshots.
legal.privacy.apps.heading: The mobile, desktop and browser apps
legal.privacy.apps.body:
**The Mahaam mobile app (iOS and Android)** has two experiences. **Staff** (owners, admins, project managers and employees) see their workspaces' projects, boards, tasks, issues and timers. **Customers** invited by a workspace see only its customer portal: the projects, requests and documents that workspace shares with them. The app keeps your sign-in token in the device's secure storage (the iOS Keychain or the Android Keystore) and some recently viewed data on the device so it opens quickly; signing out removes both. It asks for access to your camera or photos only when you choose a picture to attach or to use as your profile picture.

**The desktop tray app** starts and stops timers from your menu bar or system tray, and checks idle time as described above.

**The browser extension** reads nothing from the pages you visit. When you choose **File an issue for this page**, it sends that page's address, its title, any text you selected, and a screenshot of the visible part of the tab, which you see first and can remove. When you choose **Log time on this page**, it sends the address, title and selection, with no screenshot. Browsing normally sends nothing. Its access token is kept in memory only and is gone when you close the browser.
legal.privacy.push.heading: Push notifications
legal.privacy.push.body:
If you allow notifications on your phone, the mobile app gives us a **push token** for your device. On Android it's issued by Google **Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)**; on iPhone and iPad it's issued by **Apple Push Notification service (APNs)** and relayed through Firebase. We store the token, the platform and your app language so we can send you your notifications. A notification carries a short title and a link to the item (for example the name of a task that was assigned to you), and it passes through Google's and Apple's push services on its way to you.

In the installed web app, we store the push subscription your browser gives us, and notifications travel through your browser's push service (Google, Apple or Mozilla).

You can turn notifications off in your device or browser settings at any time. Signing out of a device, or deleting your account, removes its token.
legal.privacy.biometric.heading: Face ID and fingerprint unlock
legal.privacy.biometric.body:
In the mobile app you can choose to unlock Mahaam with Face ID, Touch ID or your fingerprint. This is optional and off until you turn it on.

It's handled entirely by your device's operating system. Mahaam only learns whether the check succeeded. **Your face or fingerprint data stays on your device**: it is never sent to us or to anyone else, and we never store it.
legal.privacy.reports.heading: Issue reports and error monitoring
legal.privacy.reports.body:
**Reporting a problem.** When someone reports a problem through Mahaam's "Report a problem" dialog, or through a feedback widget a workspace has put on its own website, the report can include a screenshot, the page address, the browser and screen size, and the page's recent console and network messages. A workspace that adds the widget to its own site is responsible for telling its visitors.

**A workspace's own error monitoring.** A workspace can connect its own software to Mahaam to receive error reports. Those reports contain whatever that software sends, and the workspace is responsible for them.

**Our own errors.** When Mahaam's servers hit an error, they report it to a Mahaam workspace that we operate, with the error message and technical details of the request, which can include your user or workspace identifier. We use this only to find and fix problems.
legal.privacy.integrations.heading: Connected services and AI agents
legal.privacy.integrations.body:
**Connected services.** If a workspace connects GitHub, Jira, Linear or Google Contacts, we store the access that service grants and the data it sends (for example repository activity or imported contacts), only to provide that feature. Disconnecting removes the access.

**AI agents.** If you create an access token for an AI agent (MCP), the agent can do only what that token allows, and never more than your own role. We record the agent's actions in the workspace's activity log like anyone else's.
legal.privacy.security.heading: Security and operation
legal.privacy.security.body:
We record when you were last active, and for every change in a workspace we record who did what and when (the activity log). Our servers keep technical logs, which include IP addresses, to keep the service running and to protect it from abuse.

Traffic to Mahaam is encrypted in transit (HTTPS). Passwords are hashed, two-factor secrets are encrypted, and each workspace's data is kept apart from every other workspace's by the database itself. No system is perfectly secure, but we work to protect your data and will tell you without undue delay if a breach affects it.
legal.privacy.analytics.heading: Analytics and crash reporting
legal.privacy.analytics.body:
We may use **Google Firebase** (Google Analytics for Firebase and Firebase Crashlytics) in the Mahaam apps to understand which features are used and to find and fix crashes.

When it's enabled, it collects things like your device model, operating system and app version, a random identifier for the app installation, your approximate location (country or city, worked out from your IP address), the screens you use and, when the app crashes, the technical state of the app at that moment.

It measures **how** Mahaam is used, never **what** is in it: task titles, project names, comments, file names and time entry descriptions are not sent. Google processes this data for us as our service provider. Where the law requires your consent, we'll ask before turning it on, and you'll be able to turn it off.
legal.privacy.cookies.heading: Cookies
legal.privacy.cookies.body:
The web app uses only the cookies it needs to work:

- `togo_session` keeps you signed in (HttpOnly, so page scripts can't read it).
- `togo_csrf` protects your forms and actions from requests made by other sites.
- `NEXT_LOCALE` remembers your language.

Your light or dark theme is remembered in your browser's local storage. There are no advertising or tracking cookies. If we ever add analytics to the web app that needs cookies, we'll list them here first and ask for your consent where the law requires it.
legal.privacy.processors.heading: Who else handles your data
legal.privacy.processors.body:
We use a small number of providers to run Mahaam, and each gets only what it needs:

- **Hosting and network** providers that run and protect our servers.
- An **email** provider for the messages we send.
- **Polar**, our merchant of record, which sells paid plans and processes payments. Polar receives the billing details you give it; we never see your full card number. If a workspace subscribes through GitHub Marketplace, GitHub handles its billing instead.
- **Google Firebase** for push notifications and, if enabled, analytics and crash reporting, and **Apple** for notifications to Apple devices.
- The **integrations** your workspace chooses to connect.

We don't sell or rent personal data. Some providers process data outside your country; where the law requires it, we rely on appropriate safeguards for those transfers. We may disclose data if the law requires it, and we'll tell you unless we're not allowed to.
legal.privacy.retention.heading: How long we keep it
legal.privacy.retention.body:
Your account and your work are kept for as long as your account and your workspaces exist. Codes we email you (to reset a password or confirm an address) expire after 10 minutes. Technical server logs and crash reports are kept for a limited time and then deleted. Push tokens are removed when you sign out of a device, when the push service tells us the token is no longer valid, or when you delete your account.

When a workspace is deleted, its work is deleted with it.
legal.privacy.deletion.heading: Deleting your account
legal.privacy.deletion.body:
You can delete your account yourself. In the mobile app, go to **Profile → Delete account**. On the web, open your profile and choose **Delete account**. You'll confirm with your password, and with a code if you use two-factor authentication.

If you're the only owner of a workspace, you'll first need to hand ownership to someone else or delete that workspace, so that one account can't take a whole team's work down with it.

When you delete your account, you're signed out everywhere at once, and every token, device and connected agent stops working. **You then have 14 days to change your mind**: signing in again during that time cancels the deletion. After 14 days the account is permanently anonymised: your email, name, picture and password are removed, and so are your memberships, inbox, devices and connections. Work you did in a shared workspace (comments, time entries on an invoice and so on) stays with that workspace, attributed to a deleted user, because it's part of other people's records.
legal.privacy.rights.heading: Your rights, copies and requests
legal.privacy.rights.body:
You can see and correct your profile in the app, change your email address or password, and delete your account at any time.

To ask for **a copy of your data** (an export), or to ask us to correct, restrict or erase something, or to object to how it's used, email [info@3x1.io](mailto:info@3x1.io) from the address on your account. We may need to confirm it's you, and we'll answer within 30 days. If the data sits in a workspace that another organisation controls, we may pass your request to its owners.

Depending on where you live, you may also have the right to complain to your local data protection authority.
legal.privacy.children.heading: Children
legal.privacy.children.body: Mahaam is a work tool and is not directed at children under 16. We don't knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 16. If you believe a child has given us personal data, email [info@3x1.io](mailto:info@3x1.io) and we'll delete it.
legal.privacy.changes.heading: Changes to this policy
legal.privacy.changes.body: When we change this policy we update the date at the top of this page. If a change matters, we'll tell you in the app or by email before it takes effect.
legal.privacy.contact.heading: Contact
legal.privacy.contact.body: For anything about privacy or your data, write to [info@3x1.io](mailto:info@3x1.io).
